traits.foliage_ranks.note: FEIS's coast Douglas-fir review: needles set spirally all round the branchlets. Abrams's genus account has them looking two-ranked by a twist, as they do on shaded shoots; the spec draws them all round.

traits.cone_retention_years.note: FEIS's coast Douglas-fir review: the cones open as they dry, most seed is down by November, and the cones stay on the tree a year or more after seedfall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 64), as Pseudotsuga mucronata: needles 20 to 30 mm, blunt, usually kept eight years; seed cones hanging, 5 to 7 cm, rarely 10.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Pseudotsuga, table 3, read): var. menziesii bears seed from 7 to 10 years, commercial collections from 20 to 25. FEIS (Uchytil 1991, read): appreciable seed from 20 to 30 years in open-grown coast Douglas-fir. The range runs from the earliest seed to appreciable crops. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 15 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set to give a plausible Douglas-fir: annual whorls of about five branches, upper branches swept up and lower ones level to drooping with upturned tips, a stiff leader, foliage kept about six years, height near 35 m at 50 years on a good site. Spray area matched to the drawn needle sprays. Not fitted to data. Cones (plant forms F3): 5 to 10 cm hang, with three-pointed bracts between the scales; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_pitch`, `cone_years`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters.

allometry.note: Rough heights and diameters for a well-stocked western Washington stand, from general forestry knowledge. Replace with a published yield or site-index table before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye. Needles stand all round the twigs (bottlebrush), unlike the flat sprays of true firs and cedars; bark thick and furrowed with a modest flare. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): needles 2 to 3 cm long and 1 to 1.5 mm wide, so a needle 0.05 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth with resin blisters when young, then very thick and deeply furrowed into dark brown ridges; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
